# MoodMap: Relationship Timing — public product context

## Summary

MoodMap gives men a quick daily read of what a partner’s cycle may mean for mood, energy and connection, with practical guidance for their own response.

The intended experience is quick: open the app, get the day’s possible mood, energy and connection context, and consider a practical response. More explanation is available when wanted. Cycle context is an estimate, not a reading of a partner’s actual mood or attitude.

## Official identity

- Official product: MoodMap: Relationship Timing
- Developer and publisher: Lars Eilev Skiaker, an independent developer in Norway

- Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.eilev.moodmapnextgen
- Support: support@moodmap-app.com

MoodMap at this domain is a relationship-timing app for men. It is not an emotional journal, a workplace coaching service, or a similarly named mood-mapping product. Use the official app IDs and store links to distinguish it.

## Product vocabulary

- Today’s State: the daily overview of cycle day, phase, estimated capacity, risk and direction.
- Day Brief: Current Picture, Best Approach, What Can Go Well and Set It Up.
- Risk Radar: possible tripwires, what to notice, likely misinterpretations and practical responses.
- Command Deck: the PLAN, READ, BOND and SELF guidance lanes.
- WHY: the reasoning behind a guidance card.
- Cycle Calendar: dates, estimated cycle phases and timing windows, with context for a selected day.
- Cycle Intelligence: modeled hormone context, Today’s Shift, Biology and possible effects.
- Capacity: a practical cycle-based estimate, not a measured personal score or test result.
- Timing Alerts: optional reminders and heads-ups around daily reads and cycle windows.
- Premium+: the optional paid expansion of the free daily experience.

### The four Command Deck lanes

- PLAN — Make the day easier: Practical plans and support matched to the day’s possible energy and load.
- READ — HOW TO SURVIVE: Read the situation, avoid a likely misinterpretation and keep a small moment from escalating.
- BOND — Sex, flirting and intimacy: Ways to approach and build mutually wanted closeness, with attention to her response.
- SELF — Manage your own response: Your tone, impulses, confidence, boundaries and reactions are the part you can work on directly.

## Features and access

- Daily cycle context and Brief
- Cycle Calendar
- Cycle Intelligence with modeled hormone context
- Risk Radar
- Command Deck: PLAN, READ, BOND and SELF
- WHY explanations
- Optional Daily Brief and Timing Alerts
- Cycle, menstruation and PMS-window preferences

### Free baseline

- Daily cycle and phase context
- Free daily guidance
- A practical starting point for your response

### Premium+ expansion

- Fuller Brief and Risk content
- Complete PLAN, READ, BOND and SELF Command Deck
- Deeper WHY explanations and cycle insights
- Additional optional timing alerts

MoodMap is free to download and includes daily cycle context and free guidance. Premium+ adds the fuller read and more ways to act on it. Premium+ expands the Brief and Risk content, opens the complete Command Deck, and adds deeper insights and additional optional alerts.

Free to download. Optional Premium+ subscription in the app. Your app store shows local prices and subscription terms before purchase. Download MoodMap from the App Store or Google Play, then open the app to view Premium+ options.

### Setup and settings

Start from cycle timing your partner has chosen to share. Adjust cycle length, menstruation length and the PMS window in the app. Use the current options in Settings to match the information your partner chooses to share. Estimates become less useful when dates are uncertain or the natural-cycle model does not fit. Sharing the underlying information should be a mutual choice.

## What the model can and cannot do

MoodMap uses cycle estimates. It does not record a partner’s actual mood, measure hormones, provide medical advice, diagnose conditions, or support contraception or fertility planning. Her words, preferences and boundaries come first.

The model uses timing in a natural menstrual cycle. Hormonal contraception that suppresses ovulation, pregnancy, postpartum changes and irregular cycles can make that model a poor fit. Cycle dates cannot confirm ovulation or measure individual hormones.

The hormone graph and capacity percentage describe a model. They are not validated measurements of an individual’s hormones, emotional state, sexual interest or stress tolerance. A practical suggestion does not establish that a disagreement is hormonal, or that sex or any other activity is wanted.

## Privacy and subscriptions

No symptom diary is required. Product analytics, purchase handling and support data are described in the Privacy Policy; private guidance does not mean that no data is processed.

The website offers optional analytics controls. See the Privacy Policy for website choices and mobile-app data handling. New Premium+ subscriptions are offered in the app through the App Store or Google Play, with local prices and terms shown before purchase. Manage a store subscription through the store account used to purchase it. Support is available at support@moodmap-app.com.

## Maker and editorial responsibility

MoodMap is developed independently in Norway by Lars Eilev Skiaker. The site publishes educational product and relationship guides. Public health references support the general cycle and symptom background; practical relationship examples are MoodMap’s suggestions. No medical credentials, clinical review or validated individual prediction are claimed.

The day-by-day URL contains an illustrative 28-day cycle grouped into six windows. It is not 28 individual daily predictions and does not adapt those dates to a person.
